text: The Lunar Roving Vehicle was driven on Apollo 15, 16, and 17, expanding lunar exploration range.
The first lunar roving drive took place on July 31, 1971 during Apollo 15 at Hadley Rille.
Designed for a top speed of about 8 mph (13 km/h), Eugene Cernan reached approximately 11.2 mph (18 km/h) on Apollo 17.
Astronaut traverses were strictly constrained by the 'walk-back limit'—the distance the crew could walk back to the Lunar Module if the rover failed.
The LRV was battery-electric, powered by two 36-volt non-rechargeable silver-zinc potassium hydroxide batteries.
All three Lunar Roving Vehicles remain parked on the Moon where their missions ended.
